```text
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.

As a user, I want to have the ability to set my event to have a specific background and foreground color. It would also be nice to have the ability to set a background picture as a substitute for a color as well.

### Describe the solution you'd like

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
-->
A setting leaflet underneath the layout leaflet that allows for setting a background/foreground color, as well as an image for the given event.



### User Story

As an event host, I want to set a background color and a text color for an event type's public booking page, so that each event looks the way I want when attendees book it.

### User Scenario

A host runs two events, "Design review" and "Coffee chat". For "Coffee chat" the host opens the event type, finds the new color setting under the layout setting, picks a warm background and a dark text color, and saves. The booking link for "Coffee chat" now shows those colors. "Design review" looks the same as before.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The event type editor has a background color setting and a text color setting under the layout setting. It is off by default.

5. After saving and reloading the editor, the pickers show the saved values.

7. If the text and background colors fail a contrast check, the editor shows a warning.

===== #13 [OPEN/] Add a waitlist for fully-booked time slots
assignees: zachbowden (Zach Bowden)
labels: enhancement, effort:high, scope: xl, type: feature
--- body ---
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

When every slot on a booking page is taken, the page is a dead end. It renders `"no_available_slots": "No available slots"` (`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:2239`) or `"all_booked_today": "All booked."` (`:735`), and the visitor leaves with nothing to do.

Two things are lost at that moment. The visitor has no way to signal that they wanted this host and this week, so they go and book elsewhere. And the host never learns that the demand existed — a fully-booked page and a page nobody visited look identical from the dashboard.

Meanwhile the product already handles the other half well: bookings get cancelled and rescheduled all the time, and those freed slots currently go to whoever happens to reload the page first.

There is no waitlist anywhere in the codebase — `rg -ni "waitlist|waiting.list"` across the repo, excluding `node_modules` and lock files, returns zero matches.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Let a visitor join a waitlist instead of hitting the dead end:

- on a fully-booked booking page, offer "join the waitlist" for a specific slot or for a date;
- when a booking is cancelled or rescheduled away, notify waitlisted people in order with a **time-limited claim link**, so a slot is not held forever by someone who has stopped watching;
- give hosts a per-event-type toggle, a cap on waitlist size, and a view of who is waiting;
- let people leave the waitlist from the notification.

This benefits both sides: attendees stop refreshing, and hosts convert cancellations into bookings instead of into gaps.

### User story

As someone trying to book a fully-booked host, I want to join a waitlist for the time I need, so that I am told when it frees up instead of having to keep checking the page.

### Rough scope

**XL.** It needs a new Prisma model and migration, a hook into the cancel and reschedule paths to detect a released slot, notification delivery, an expiring claim flow that has to resolve a race between claimants, host settings UI, attendee UI, and i18n — and it must respect `EventType.seatsPerTimeSlot` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:222`) rather than assuming one booking per slot.

### Source

Reviewing the booking page's own empty-state strings while verifying the local setup on 2026-09-14: the product ships copy for "all booked" and has nothing behind it.

### Additional context

Intended labels: `type: feature`, `scope: xl`. Nearest existing labels: `enhancement`, `effort:high`. I do n

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Bookings is a flat list of Upcoming/Past/Cancelled. There is no way to see an overview of the month in the style of a calendar.


### Describe the solution you'd like

As a host, I want a week and month view of my bookings, so I can see how my time is actually shaped instead of reading a list.


### Describe alternatives you've considered

<!--
  Let us know about other solutions you've tried or researched.
-->

Weekly view already exists but is not enabled by default. Add monthly view and enable by default in bookings page. Personal use; every calendar tool has this and cal.diy doesn't.

### Requirement/Document

<!--
  Is there any type of document that could support that feature?
-->

## User Story
As a host, I want a month view of my bookings next to the existing list and week views, so that I can see how my month is shaped at a glance instead of reading a list.

## User Scenario
A host on a desktop browser opens Bookings for the first time with no saved view. The page opens in Month: a seven-column grid of every week that touches the current month, starting on the host's preferred first weekday, with days from the previous and next month greyed out and today highlighted. Each day lists its bookings with start time and title, placed on the day they start in the host's selected timezone. The host clicks a booking and the existing booking details panel opens for it. The host moves to next month with the arrow, comes back with Today, and switches to Week or List with the view toggle. After reloading, the page opens on the last view the host chose.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The view toggle shows List, Week and Month. `?view=calendar` still opens the existing weekly view and `?view=month` opens the month grid.
2. A desktop user with the bookings calendar enabled, no `?view=` in the URL and no saved view opens in Month. A valid `?view=` value wins over a saved view, a saved view wins over the Month default, and an invalid value in either place is ignored.
3. On screens 768px wide or narrower, and for users without the bookings calendar enabled, the list view is shown as before.
4. The month grid shows every week containing a day of the month, seven days per week, starting on the user's first weekday (Sunday or Monday), for 28-, 29-, 30- and 31-day mon

assignees: dbbeynam (Demir Beynam)
labels: enhancement, effort:medium, scope: medium, type: feature
--- body ---
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Every booking action is one-at-a-time. Clearing a day before you travel, cancelling a week of meetings when you're ill, or marking a run of no-shows all mean opening each booking separately and repeating the same reason into each one.

### Describe the solution you'd like

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
-->

As a host who needs to clear a day, I want to select several bookings and cancel them together with a single message to the attendees, so that I don't repeat the same action and the same explanation ten times.

## User Story
As a host who needs to clear a day, I want to select several of my upcoming bookings and cancel them together with one shared reason, so that I don't repeat the same action and the same explanation for every booking.

## User Scenario
A host is ill and needs to clear tomorrow. On the Upcoming bookings tab they tick the checkboxes next to their three meetings for tomorrow. A bar appears showing "3 selected" with "Clear selection" and "Cancel selected". They click "Cancel selected", and a dialog lists the three bookings and asks for a cancellation reason. They type "Sorry, I'm ill and need to cancel today" and confirm. Each booking is cancelled one after another through the same cancellation the single "Cancel event" action uses, so each booking's attendees get their usual cancellation email with that reason. If one cancellation fails, the others still go through, the dialog shows how many succeeded and failed with the error for each failure, and "Retry failed" tries only the failed ones again.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. On the Upcoming tab, a checkbox appears only on bookings the signed-in user hosts that are accepted, have not ended, and whose event type allows cancelling. Other users' bookings, unconfirmed, past and cancelled bookings, and the "Today"/"Next" separator rows have no checkbox. Other tabs show no checkboxes.
2. Clicking a checkbox selects or deselects that booking and does not open the booking details panel.
3. "Select all on this page" selects every eligible booking on the current page, up to 10. Bookings on other pages are never selected.
4. Changing page, page size, filters or status tab clears the selection.
5. "Cancel selected" opens a dialog listing the selected bookings. Closing the dialog without confirming cancels nothing.
6. The confirm button is disabled while the reason is empty or only spaces, and while a batch is runn

===== #63 [OPEN/] Day-of-Week Recurrence Selection
assignees: dchan01-wm (Dylan Han)
labels: enhancement, effort:medium
--- body ---
## User Story
As an event host, I want to configure weekly recurring events to repeat on specific days (e.g., Tuesday and Thursday).

## User Scenario
An event host configures a weekly recurring event, selecting specific days (e.g., Tuesday and Thursday) from a new toggle row. When a booker schedules the event, they only see availability for those selected days. 

## Acceptance Criteria
1. When setting an event to repeat weekly, a new row of buttons (Sunday through Saturday) appears, allowing the host to select specific days.
2. The system requires at least one day to be selected and prevents users from unchecking every day.
3. The selected days are successfully saved to the event's settings so they apply to all future bookings.
4. Automated tests must ensure the calendar correctly generates the schedule based on the chosen days.

## Out of Scope
- Implementing specific end dates ("Ends: Never / On [date]")—the system will continue using a maximum occurrence count.
- Day-of-week selection for monthly or yearly recurrence intervals.
- Updating the `GoogleCalendarService` sync logic to support the new day selection (to be handled in a follow-up issue).

## Open Question
- Does the "maximum of N events" limit refer to individual meetings or total weeks (e.g., does a max of 8 on a Tue/Thu schedule mean 4 weeks or 8 weeks)?

===== #93 [CLOSED/COMPLETED] Add long-press to start drag on touch devices in the weekly availability grid
assignees: julissaehp
labels: enhancement, effort:medium
--- body ---
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Since #70, the weekly availability grid supports drag-to-select with mouse and touch. On touch devices, a finger on any day cell **always** starts a selection, because the cells use `touch-action: none` so the browser doesn't scroll while dragging.

On a phone the grid fills most of the screen. A user who puts a finger on the grid to **scroll** (the page, or the grid's own 600px scroll area) selects or deselects time slots by accident. Scrolling currently only works by dragging on the hour-label column or the day header, which users aren't likely to discover. We made this decision to constrain the scope of earlier PRs, but this issue arose.

As an event host on a phone, I'm frustrated when I try to scroll through my week and end up changing my availability instead.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Use **long-press to start a drag on touch input**, the way Google Calendar's mobile app works:

- **Swipe** on the grid: scrolls normally (page or grid), with no selection.
- **Press and hold** a cell for about 350ms without moving: the starting cell highlights to show a drag has started. Dragging then selects or deselects exactly as in #70: the starting cell's state sets the mode, the drag stays in that day's column, and the grid auto-scrolls near its edges.
- **Mouse and pen:** unchanged, the drag starts immediately on press.

Acceptance criteria:
1. On touch devices, a quick swipe starting on a grid cell scrolls and never changes the selection.
2. On touch devices, holding a cell for about 350ms, then dragging, selects or deselects slots with the same behavior as #70, including auto-scroll.
3. Once a long-press drag has started, the page and grid don't scroll under the finger, except for the grid's own edge auto-scroll.
4. A long press doesn't open the browser's context menu, the iOS callout, or a text selection.
5. Mouse behavior is unchanged.
6. Automated tests cover the hold threshold, cancelling on movement, and mouse versus touch behavior.

Implementation notes (from the #70 design):
- **Where:** the logic belongs in `packages/features/schedules/hooks/useWeeklyGridDrag.ts`.
- **Starting the timer:** on a touch `pointerdown`, start a timer instead of a drag. Cancel it if the finger moves more than about 8px first, or if the browser takes over scrolling (it fires `pointercancel`).
- **Blocking scroll once dragging:** add a native `touchmove` listener with `{ passive: false }` that calls `preventDefault()`. R

===== #104 [CLOSED/COMPLETED] Show the away badge and redirect for partial-day out-of-office entries
assignees: zach-short (Zachary Short)
labels: enhancement, effort:medium
--- body ---

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

PR #85 (closes #6) lets a host set a leave time and a return time on an out-of-office entry. The booking page now removes the slots inside that window, but it does that the way it removes a calendar event: the slots are gone, and nothing says why. A whole-day entry shows the "away" panel with the reason, the emoji, the public note and, when a redirect user is set, a "Book with <name>" button. A partial-day entry shows none of these. PR #85 names this as a known limit ("Partial-day entries do not show the "away" badge or a redirect on the booking page") and describes "alternative 1" as the path to fix it.

### Describe the solution you would like

Build alternative 1 from PR #85: teach the per-day out-of-office map about time ranges. Slots inside a partial-day window stay in the slot list, marked `away` with the entry's reason, emoji, note and redirect user, the same data a whole-day entry carries. The booker then renders one "away" panel at the place in the day where the window falls, between the slots before it and the slots after it. Away slots stay unbookable, as they are for whole days today.

### User Story

As an attendee who opens a host's booking page, I want to see that the host is away for part of the day, and book with their redirect user if one is set, so that I know why some times are missing and where to book instead.

### User Scenario

A host works 09:00 to 17:00 and has a partial-day entry from 14:00 to 16:00 with the reason "Doctor" and a public note. An attendee opens the booking page for that day. Slots from 09:00 run up to the slot that ends at 14:00. Below them is the away panel with the emoji, the reason and the note. Below the panel, slots resume at 16:00. If the entry has a redirect user, the panel also shows "Book with <name>", and the button opens that user's booking page on the same date.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. For a partial-day entry, every slot that overlaps the window is returned with `away: true` and the entry's `fromUser`, `toUser`, `reason`, `emoji`, and the note when `showNotePublicly` is on. Slots that do not overlap the window have no `away` flag.
2. A slot marked away for a partial-day entry cannot be booked. Booking it returns the same error as booking inside a whole-day entry.
3. On the booking page, a day with a partial-day window shows the bookable slots before the window, one away panel, and the bookable slots after the window, in that order. This holds when the w

===== #111 [CLOSED/COMPLETED] Add an admin setting to require 2FA for all users
assignees: kojoshuay
labels: 
--- body ---
## User Story
As a site admin, I want a setting that requires two-factor authentication for every user, so that I can enforce one security policy across my whole cal.diy installation.

## User Scenario
A site admin opens the admin settings page and sees a "Require two-factor authentication for all users" toggle. Turning it on saves the setting for the whole site, and the toggle stays on after the page reloads. Regular users can't see or change it. This issue only stores and manages the setting. Making users set up 2FA is handled in sub-issue 2.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The application securely stores a site-wide 2FA enforcement setting that defaults to "off," utilizing a storage method that preserves all existing application data.
2. Only users with site administrator privileges can view or modify the setting. The backend must strictly reject any read or write attempts from non-admins or unauthenticated users.
3. The admin settings area provides a clear, interactive control (e.g., a toggle) to manage the global 2FA requirement.
4. The UI accurately displays the current saved state of the setting
5. Automated tests verify that the setting persists correctly across sessions and that the admin-only security boundary cannot be bypassed.

## Out of Scope
- Requiring users to set up 2FA (sub-issue 2)
- A per-team version of the setting
- Turning off users' existing 2FA when the setting is turned off

===== #112 [CLOSED/COMPLETED] Require users to set up 2FA when the admin setting is on
assignees: kojoshuay
labels: 
--- body ---
## User Story

As a site admin, I want users without 2FA to be required to set it up, so that the setting actually protects every account.

## User Scenario

The setting is on. A user who logs in with a password and doesn't have 2FA sees a setup window that can't be closed. They go through the existing setup steps: confirm their password, scan the QR code, enter the 6-digit code and save their backup codes. Then they use the app normally. A new user who signs up with email and password has to complete a 2FA step during onboarding. Users who sign in with Google or another provider aren't affected. When the setting is off, nothing changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At login, the server decides whether the user must set up 2FA and stores the result in their session. All three conditions must hold: the setting is on, the user doesn't have 2FA, and the user signs in with a password. The browser can't skip this check.

2. While setup is required, a 2FA setup window appears on every page. It reuses the existing setup steps and has no Cancel or Close button.

3. After finishing setup, the user can use the app normally.

4. When the setting is on, onboarding includes a required 2FA step for users who sign up with a password. Otherwise the step is skipped.

5. Users who sign in through Google or another identity provider are exempt, since they can't set up 2FA in cal.diy.

6. Write tests for the login rule, covering each of the three conditions, and for the onboarding step.

## Out of Scope

* Storing or toggling the setting (sub-issue 1)
* Forcing setup on users who were already logged in when the setting was turned on. The rule applies at their next login.
* A per-team version of the setting
* Changes to how 2FA itself works

===== #117 [OPEN/] Choose which weekdays a weekly recurring event repeats on
assignees: dchan01-wm (Dylan Han)
labels: enhancement, effort:medium
--- body ---
### Is your proposal related to a problem?
(edited issue description)

A weekly recurring event can only repeat on the weekday of the first booking. A host who holds sessions on Tuesday and Thursday can't offer one recurring event that covers both days, so a client has to book two separate series.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add a row of day buttons to the Recurring tab for weekly events. Save the selected days with the event type, together with the host's time zone and start of week, and use them when the series of bookings is generated, so "Tuesday" always means Tuesday for the host. The server also rejects a series whose first slot isn't on a selected day. Details are in the User Story and Acceptance Criteria below.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- **Two event types** (one for Tuesday, one for Thursday): works today, but the client books twice and the two series aren't linked.
- **Host pre-creates open sessions that anyone can book:** "which days I'm open" is already covered by the weekly Availability schedule, and pre-made sessions would need a new data model and booking flow. Not chosen.
- **Judge weekdays in the booker's time zone:** simpler for the booking page, but a host's Tuesday 10 PM session would become a Wednesday for bookers further east, so the series wouldn't match the host's plan. Not chosen.
- **Look up the host's time zone at booking time instead of saving it with the rule:** always current, but the booking page and the server would both need extra data, and team events would need a rule for whose zone counts. Not chosen for now (see Out of Scope).

### Additional context

This is the host side of #63, which is split into two sub-issues: this one (choose and save the days, generate the series, reject a first slot on an unselected day) and #118 (only offer the selected days on the booking page), which is merged after this one. Both are part of #23. End conditions are #64. If time runs short this sprint, acceptance criterion 5 moves to #118.

### Requirement/Document

- Notion Calendar recurrence screenshot in #63 and #23.
- RFC 5545 RRULE `BYDAY` (weekly recurrence on specific weekdays) and `WKST` (the day a week starts on, which matters for "every 2 weeks"), both supported by the existing `rrule` library.

## User Story
As an event host, I want to choose which days of the week my weekly recurring event repeats on (e.g. Tuesday and Thursday) so that one booking gives my client a series on exactly the days I hold
```

```text
1:# Issue Summaries and Difficulty Estimates
39:- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** The work spans the database (new columns need approval, or the existing `eventTypeColor` JSON gets extended), the event type editor UI, and the booker's styling via `use-brand-colors.tsx`, for about 6–8 files. The logic itself is simple: hex validation, a contrast check, and conditionally applying CSS variables to one event type's booking page. The existing `eventTypeColor` pattern (storage, toggle, contrast warning strings) gives a template, which keeps this from going higher, but open questions about light/dark theme conflicts add some design work.
44:- **Estimated difficulty: 4/10.** It needs a new Prisma enum and column plus a migration, a dropdown in the Advanced tab, validation on the reschedule path, and tests, so it touches the schema, the event type UI and the booking backend. The full pattern already exists end to end for cancellation reasons (`CancellationReasonRequirement`, `handleCancelBooking.ts`), so most of the work is a parallel copy of known-good code. The main risk is finding every reschedule entry point (attendee-initiated vs. host "request reschedule") so that the validation can't be bypassed.
47:## #12 — `yarn build` silently migrates the database `DATABASE_URL` points at
49:- **Estimated difficulty: 2/10.** The fix touches two files: widening the `catch` in `is-prisma-available-check.ts` and adding a warning line to `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The only subtle part is recognizing connection-refused errors (e.g. Prisma's `P1001`-style errors) as "unavailable" without hiding real failures. A small unit test for the guard is straightforward to write.
50:- **Summary:** The documented `yarn build` step runs `prisma migrate deploy` against whatever database `DATABASE_URL` points at, so it can silently migrate a shared or staging database. Separately, the "no database, skip migrations" guard only catches `PrismaClientInitializationError`, so a refused connection crashes the build with a misleading error. The proposed fix makes connection failures count as "unavailable" and documents the migration side effect.
54:- **Estimated difficulty: 9/10.** This touches nearly every layer: a new Prisma model and migration, hooks in the cancel and reschedule paths, notification delivery, host settings UI, attendee-facing UI on the booking page, and i18n. The logic is hard because the time-limited claim links need race resolution between claimants, and the feature has to respect `seatsPerTimeSlot` instead of assuming one booking per slot. It would need to be split into several PRs to stay within the repo's size limits.
59:- **Estimated difficulty: 8/10.** It needs a new repository, service and tRPC router following the layering rules, a new App Router route, charts, date and team filters, i18n and tests, so it is many files across many packages. The aggregate queries over `Booking` must be indexed and non-quadratic to scale. A chart library may also be a new dependency, which needs approval first.
64:- **Estimated difficulty: 8/10.** Locations are stored as JSON on `EventType`, so linking each one to a schedule needs a schema or JSON-shape change, editor UI, and changes to slot calculation, which then has to take the selected location as input. The booker must re-fetch slots when the location changes, and booking-time validation must also check the location's schedule, or bookings could get around it. The core availability engine is sensitive, and team or round-robin events with multiple hosts add edge cases.
69:- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** Storing recurrence (frequency, interval, end date) on overrides needs a schema change, plus updates to the override dialog UI and the availability calculation that expands overrides into date ranges. The availability logic has to decide whether a recurring override applies to a given date, correctly across timezones and DST. Unresolved questions about editing whole series, deleting single occurrences, and conflicts with one-off overrides could significantly expand the scope.
74:- **Estimated difficulty: 3/10.** It needs a stored preference (a new `User` column, which needs schema approval, or a field in user metadata), a dropdown in account settings, a tRPC input change, and an update to the post-login redirect. That is about 4–6 files with simple logic. The main care point is precedence, since an explicit `callbackUrl` should still win over the saved default.
79:- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** This changes the recurrence UI, the `recurringEvent` data shape and RRule generation, and the code that creates and checks every occurrence of a recurring booking, so it affects the editor, the booker and the booking engine. Calendar integrations and emails that consume the recurrence rule also need to stay consistent. Much of this scope has since been split into #63 (day-of-week) and #64 (end conditions), so this issue mostly works as an umbrella.
84:- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** This fork has no workflows module (`packages/features/ee/workflows` is absent), so it needs new scheduling infrastructure (a delayed job via the tasker/Trigger.dev pattern or a cron), plus reminder settings, schema changes and a new email template. Reminders must be cancelled or rescheduled whenever the booking changes, which adds hooks in several booking paths. Sending at the right time across timezones and with retries adds reliability concerns.
89:- **Estimated difficulty: 3/10.** This is a frontend change, mostly in the signup form: switching validation to run on change or blur and showing the existing error indicators sooner. Password and email format checks are local, but "username taken" needs a debounced async availability check against an existing or new endpoint. No database changes are needed, and only about 1–3 files.
94:- **Estimated difficulty: 8/10.** It needs a new dependency (an LLM or embedding provider, which needs approval), an API endpoint, a searchable index of every settings page and option, and a search UI with results or walkthroughs. Self-hosted instances add configuration, API-key handling, cost and graceful fallback when AI is off. The index must also stay in sync as settings change, and LLM answers need guarding against pointing users at settings that don't exist.
99:- **Estimated difficulty: 3/10.** The logic is trivial: a `formatDuration(minutes, t)` helper built on the existing, tested `minutesToHoursAndMinutes`. It does touch about 5 display sites (event type badge, multiple-durations dropdown, editor subtitle, two onboarding views), plus a new i18n string and tests. One call site (the "Basics" subtitle) still needs to be found.
104:- **Estimated difficulty: 6/10.** Mostly a frontend change: a new month-grid component, a three-way view toggle, URL vs. saved-view precedence, and default-view logic for desktop only, for about 6–8 files. Placing bookings on the correct day in the selected timezone (midnight, DST, recurring occurrences) and loading more than 100 bookings per month take careful logic and testing. No schema or API changes are needed, which keeps it out of the high range.
109:- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** The "Book again" button alone is small (about a 2/10), because the booker already accepts prefilled name and email through URL parameters. The "People" view raises it: a new page plus a query that groups past attendees by email with counts and last-meeting dates. The issue has no acceptance criteria, so the scope has to be decided before implementation.
114:- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** It is frontend-only and reuses the existing `/api/cancel` endpoint, but touches the bookings data table (a checkbox column with eligibility rules), selection state, a selection bar and a confirmation dialog. The batch logic needs sequential requests, a 10-item cap matching the rate limit, partial-failure reporting and "retry failed only" behavior. About 5–7 files including tests.
119:- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** It needs a new soft-cancel state (a schema change), an undo toast, and a background job to finalize the cancellation after the grace period. Cancellation has many side effects (attendee emails, calendar event deletion, webhooks, refunds), and they must all be delayed until the cancellation is final, which means restructuring a critical path. Whether the slot is open or held during the grace period is another subtle decision.
124:- **Estimated difficulty: 4/10.** The fix is probably small: let signup reclaim a username held by an unverified, abandoned account, or clean that account up when the user chooses "use a different email". It needs reproduction and careful conditions so a verified user's username can never be taken over. About 2–4 files plus a test.
129:- **Estimated difficulty: 6/10.** It adds a day-of-week field to the `recurringEvent` JSON (RRule already supports `byweekday`), a row of day toggles in the recurrence UI, and changes to how occurrence dates are generated and booked. Occurrence generation, the booker's display of recurring dates, and the meaning of the occurrence count all need to stay consistent. Google Calendar sync is deferred, but the RRule must still not break other integrations.
134:- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** It adds an "Ends" section (Never / On date / After N times) to the recurrence UI and an `until` field to the recurrence data, which RRule already supports. "Never" is harder than it looks, because recurring bookings are created as individual rows, so an infinite series needs a cap or a different model. The issue is light on acceptance criteria, which adds some scope uncertainty.
139:- **Estimated difficulty: 3/10.** Admin 2FA is already enforced in production: `next-auth-options.ts` downgrades admins without 2FA to `INACTIVE_ADMIN`, and `AdminPasswordBanner` prompts them. Most of the work is a toggle (for example a `Feature` flag row with a migration and an admin settings switch) and turning the banner into a non-dismissable prompt when it's on. That is a few files across auth and admin settings, with simple logic.
144:- **Estimated difficulty: 6/10.** Unlike #67, there's no existing enforcement for regular users, so it needs a session flag, app-wide gating (e.g. middleware or a shell guard) that blocks use until 2FA is set up, and a required 2FA step in signup. It touches the instance settings, the auth/session layer, the shell UI and the onboarding flow. Edge cases include SSO/OAuth users and API access, and lockout risk makes thorough testing important.
149:- **Estimated difficulty: 2/10.** This is a visibility toggle (a "Text / Visual" segmented control) in one component (`AvailabilitySettings.tsx`), with session-level persistence and new i18n strings. It deliberately does not handle data consistency, which is #72. The only dependency is that the grid component from #69 exists.
154:- **Estimated difficulty: 6/10.** It touches only a few frontend files, but it is the most logic-heavy part of the epic: two-way conversion between cell-based grid state and range-based intervals in one shared source of truth. Non-contiguous blocks, overnight ranges and rounding to the grid's cell size are all edge cases that can lose data. It has to work with the existing form state and needs thorough unit tests on the conversion functions.
159:- **Estimated difficulty: 4/10.** Because it keeps the existing save endpoint and payload format, this is mostly verification: the grid must produce identical payloads, and loaded data must fill both views. The work is mostly regression testing of the text-field save/load path plus small fixes in the form's serialization. The text says it depends on #71, but the shared state it relies on comes from #72, so that dependency should be clarified.
160:- **Summary:** Availability set in the new grid will not persist unless the save/load flow handles the shared data model. The issue requires the API payload to be identical whether the user saved from grid or text mode, and loaded data to fill both views correctly. A separate grid-specific endpoint was rejected in favor of one endpoint and one data format.
164:- **Estimated difficulty: 5/10.** The change lives in about 3 files (`useWeeklyGridDrag.ts`, `WeeklyAvailabilityGrid.tsx`, tests), but low-level pointer-event handling is fiddly. It needs a hold timer cancelled by movement or `pointercancel`, a non-passive native `touchmove` listener to block scrolling once dragging, and suppression of the iOS callout and context menu. jsdom can't simulate real scrolling, so it also needs manual testing on a device.
169:- **Estimated difficulty: 7/10.** It touches the core availability engine (`getUserAvailability.ts`, `date-ranges.ts`, `slots.ts`), changes the `IOutOfOfficeData` shape to carry time windows, and reworks the booker components so the away panel can appear mid-day. That is about 5 code files plus 4 test files, close to the PR limit, and the issue itself suggests splitting engine and booker work. DST handling, keeping bookings blocked inside the window, and the open question about multiple entries per day all add risk.
```

```text
reviews: dchan01-wm(APPROVED)

## What does this PR do?

- Closes #104

Since PR #85 a host can be away for part of a day. The booking page removed those slots and said nothing, so an attendee saw a gap with no reason and no "Book with" link. A whole-day entry already shows the "away" panel with the emoji, the reason, the public note and the redirect. This PR gives a partial-day entry the same panel, in the place in the day where the window falls. This is "alternative

**The slot engine.** A partial-day window now stays in the host's `dateRanges`, so its slots are generated and then marked `away`, the same path a whole day takes. The window is still subtracted from `oooExcludedDateRanges`, which is what `ensureAvailableUsers` checks a booking against, so an away slot cannot be booked (criterion 2). The per-day away map (`IOutOfOfficeData`) keeps one record per d

**Slot marking.** `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` marks a slot on a windowed date away only when the slot overlaps a window: `slotStart < windowEnd && slotEnd > windowStart`. Any overlap counts (criterion 1), so a slot that straddles the leave time is away too, which matches what the booking guard rejects. Whole-day marking is unchanged. The windows are parsed to numbers once per `getSlots` call.

**The booker.** `AvailableTimes` renders one away panel at the first slot of each run of away slots and hides the away slots, so the panel sits between the slots before and after the window (criterion 3). Two windows on one day give two panels. The panel keeps today's text; no new string. The "Book with" button already works from the slot's `toUser`, so the redirect needs only the data (criterion 

**Decisions, from the issue's open questions.** Any overlap marks a slot away, because the fully-inside rule would show slots the booking guard then rejects. The panel keeps today's text; its place between the slots shows the window, and that is also the answer for attendees far from the host's zone. Two windows give two panels. Criterion 4 stays, shown by a unit test; the redirect switch in the f

## Design

**Decision.** Keep the away map keyed by date and hang the windows under the date record. Whole days and partial days then share one map, one lookup in the slot engine and one set of booker readers.

**Alternatives considered.**

1. A separate map of windows next to `datesOutOfOffice`. Every consumer of the map (the slot engine, the tRPC slots util, the onboarding hook) would take a second argument, and the whole-day-wins rule would live in two places.
2. One record per window with the date record replaced by a list. Every reader of `IOutOfOfficeData["anyDate"]` in the booker and the `DatePicker` would change shape for a feature that most days never use.
3. Mark only slots fully inside the window. A slot that straddles the leave time would look bookable and fail at booking time, a silent error.

**Rationale.** The windowed record is additive: a date without `windows` is exactly what it was before, so existing tests pass unchanged (criterion 6), and the engine keeps the whole-day and partial-day split that PR #85 introduced. Windows are read from the same `wallClockToTimeZone` parse, so the DST behaviour is the one already tested.

**Consequences.** `SlotInfo` in `packages/features/calendars/lib/types.ts` still lists no `notes`, though the server sends it and the panel shows it; the new booker test widens the type locally and the component is left alone. `buildDateRanges` now skips windowed dates when it removes whole days from `oooExcludedDateRanges`; without that line a windowed date lost all of its bookable ranges, which

- **Environment variables:** none beyond a normal local setup.
- **Test data:** the seed (`yarn db-seed`). Log in as `pro` (Europe/London). The `OutOfOfficeEntry` table starts empty.
- **Happy path:**

  2. Open `/pro/30min` on that date in Europe/London. Slots run 9:00am to 1:30pm, then the away panel with the emoji, "Pro Example is OOO" and the note, then 4:00pm and 4:30pm (criteria 1 and 3).

  6. Make an all-day entry on another day. It looks as before (criterion 6).
- **Automated** (`TZ=UTC`, and the timezone test also under `VITEST_MODE=timezone`):
  - `date-ranges.test.ts`: the windows helper, including a window past midnight and two windows on the 2026-03-08 DST change in America/New_York.
  - `slots.test.ts`: windows at the start, middle and end of a day, a straddling slot, a window shorter than a slot, two windows, a window covering the working day, and the DST day.
  - `getUserAvailability.outOfOffice.timezone.test.ts`: the ranges split, the away map, the slots a booker gets, a window past midnight, the DST day, and whole-day-wins.
  - `ensureAvailableUsers.outOfOffice.test.ts`: a booking inside the window and one straddling the leave time are rejected with the same error as a whole-day entry; bookings that end at the leave time or start at the return time are accepted.
  - `AvailableTimes.test.tsx`: panel order for start, middle and end windows, two panels for two windows, the all-away day, the redirect button's target, and the public note.

===== #113 MERGED kojoshuay +7848/-17 files:18 mergedBy:kojoshuay
implement issue 111 for admins have the ability to toggle on/off 2FA …
reviews: zachbowden(APPROVED)
requested:
## What does this PR do?
- Closes #111 
- implements a Security settings page allowing Admins to enforce site-wide 2FA. It stores this setting as a live-read feature flag to bypass stale caches, pairing it with UI confirmation safeguards and backend authorization checks.

**What changed**
* Seeded the require-two-factor-auth feature flag via database migration and registered the slug in TypeScript configs.
* Added `getPrismaFeatureRepository()` to the DI container and created the `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide` helper to bypass the cache and safely read the live database.
* Built the /settings/admin/security page with ADMIN session verification and added its link to the admin sidebar.
* Created the security-view component to handle the toggle switch, the warning dialog safeguard, and the tRPC network mutation.
* Hid the new 2FA flag from the generic FlagAdminList to ensure admins can only modify it through the secure page.

**Motivation and context (Design Decisions)**
For the data storage design, I considered three options before choosing the final approach:
1. **A new column on the `Deployment` table:** While this table handles installation-wide settings, adding a new `requireTwoFactorAuth` boolean was rejected because it would require building entirely new repository methods, endpoints, and admin checks from scratch.
2. **A new dedicated `SiteSettings` table:** This would involve creating a brand new one-row model specifically for security policies. I rejected this option as over-engineering for a single boolean, as it demanded the most upfront work, including a new schema migration, repository, interface, and DI container.
3. **A row in the existing `Feature` table (Chosen):** The application already uses this exact pattern for other site-wide authentication rules (like `email-verification` and `disable-signup`). I chose this option because it required zero schema changes—only a data seed migration—allowing me to safely reuse existing backend architecture.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** None.

**Encountered:** I encountered a caching trap where the feature repository uses a 5-minute cache, meaning reads could be up to 5 minutes out of date. I handled this by modifying the DI container file to import the existing `PrismaFeatureRepository` recipe and building a new getter function so the 2FA check can request live, uncached repository reads.

## What does this PR do?

- Fixes #93

This PR improves touch interactions in the weekly availability grid by adding long-press functionality for selecting and deselecting time slots.

Previously, swiping on the calendar using a touchscreen could accidentally select time slots instead of scrolling. This made navigating the availability grid difficult on touch devices.

**Changes made:**
- Added a 350ms long-press delay before touch dragging begins.
- Added an 8px movement tolerance to distinguish scrolling from selection.
- Allowed users to scroll normally with quick finger swipes.
- Preserved quick tapping to select or deselect individual time slots.
- Prevented unwanted scrolling and context menus during active touch dragging.
- Preserved same-day selection and automatic scrolling near the grid edges.
- Added cancellation when a second finger touches the grid, preventing accidental selections during multi-touch gestures.
- Maintained existing mouse and pen interaction behavior.
- Updated the weekly availability grid styling and automated tests.

No additional dependencies were required.


## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

The multi-touch cancellation logic currently detects a second finger only when it touches a time slot within the weekly availability grid. If the second finger touches a day header or another part of the page, the active drag may continue. A page-wide pointer listener could address this limitation in the future, but I kept the implementation scoped to the grid to avoid introducing unnecessary glob

**Encountered:**

The existing drag-to-select functionality was designed to start immediately when a user pressed a time slot, which caused touch gestures to select availability instead of allowing normal scrolling. I addressed this by introducing a 350ms long-press delay and an 8px movement tolerance for touch interactions while preserving the existing mouse and pen behavior..
```

```text
requested:
### What does this PR do?
- Closes #112
- Enforces the site-wide mandatory 2FA by intercepting existing users with an inescapable setup modal and routing new users through a dedicated 2FA setup step during their initial onboarding.

### What changed
- Added `requiresTwoFactorSetup.ts` helper to efficiently check 2FA requirements using the Redis cache and early exits.
- Extended NextAuth `User` and `JWT` interfaces in `next-auth.d.ts` for the custom `requiresTwoFactorSetup` flag.
- Updated `next-auth-options.ts` to append the flag at login, persist it in the session, and reorder `autoMergeIdentities` so live backend reads overwrite stale cookies.
- Secured the NextAuth `update()` session trigger to verify user IDs directly against the live database.
- Locked down `EnableTwoFactorModal` with an `isRequired` prop to remove cancel options and background dismissals.
- Added the `require_2fa_setup_notice` translation to `common.json`.
- Created `RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal` and mounted it globally in `Shell.tsx` for inescapable site-wide enforcement.
- Added the `useFinishPersonalOnboarding` hook to intercept new user setups and dynamically expand onboarding to 3 steps.
- Built `PersonalTwoFactorView` for the new onboarding step, ensuring the session refreshes before completion.
- Created a server-side gatekeeper (`/onboarding/personal/two-factor/page.tsx`) to block unauthorized access to the setup route.

### Motivation and context (Design Decisions)
For the session state and enforcement mechanism, I considered three options before choosing the final approach:
1. **Option A (Sign out and back in):** Once a user finishes setting up 2FA, the system forcefully logs them out, forcing them to log back in to issue a fresh token. I rejected this because it causes the user to enter passwords and 2FA codes multiple times.
2. **Option B (Refresh the session in place):** The browser asks the server to update the current token right after setup. I rejected this because a user could manipulate their browser console to tell the server they no longer need 2FA. 
3. **Option C (Recalculate on Every Session Read) (Chosen):** On every session read (e.g., `getServerSession`), the server dynamically recalculates the 2FA requirement, ignoring and overriding any stale flag data stored in the browser's cookie. I chose this because it resolves state-sync issues without forcing session termination. If an admin toggles the site-wide rule or a user enables 2FA on a m

### Tech Debt
* **Introduced:** None.
* **Encountered:** Stale client-side session tokens from policy changes or multi-device setups were resolved by overriding NextAuth cookies with live calculations in `autoMergeIdentities` and re-verifying user IDs on `update()` triggers. Additionally, a race condition where background tab refreshes prematurely closed the setup modal was fixed using a local state-latch in `RequiredTwoFactorSetupMod
```

```text
## Deliverables, points and deadlines

Sprint 2 is worth 100 points (10% of the course grade); 78 are individual (including the 8-point survey) and 22 are team-graded. A team with no merged PRs, no sprint report, or no release gets 0 for the whole sprint.

All deadlines are 11:59 PM. Extra credit: up to 3 bonus points per PR accepted or under active review in the real upstream project.

## Things that must improve (graded strictly)

These five problems were seen in Sprint 1 and will cost points in Sprint 2.

1. **AI log completeness.** Every student commits logs. Each log has both your prompts and the AI's full output. Summaries, or output without prompts, lose credit.
2. **AI log linking.** For every issue or PR that involved AI, post a comment on that issue or PR linking directly to the specific log file. A link to the folder, or to a different issue/PR, does not count. Sprint 2 accepts the comment on either the issue or the PR.
3. **AI log format.** SpecStory format is strongly recommended. Screenshots are not logs.
4. **No self-reviews.** You cannot approve or merge your own PR. Reviewers post substantive comments, not just an approval. Notify your reviewer in Zulip (or email) and aim to review within 24 hours of being asked.
5. **Design alternatives.** Each design decision names at least two concrete options and why one won. "We decided to use X" alone loses credit.
```

```markdown
# Sprint 3 Outlook and Plan

Based on the Sprint 2 milestone, PRs and backlog as of 2026-10-30. Owner assignments and story points below are **suggestions for the team to confirm in planning**, not decisions. Sprint 3 deliverables are assumed to match Sprint 2's (backlog, specs, design decisions, PRs, AI logs, diagrams, check-in, report, release); adjust once the Sprint 3 brief is out.

## 1. Where Sprint 2 left us

| | Sprint 2 result |
|---|---|
| Issues in milestone | 13 |
| Closed | 6 (#71, #93, #104, #111, #112, and #57, which was closed after the first report table was drafted) |
| Suggested points closed | 31 of 74 (42%) |
| Feature PRs merged | 7 (#110, #113, #114, #115, #116, #120, and #125, merged Oct 30 at about 1:40 AM ET, after the deadline) |
| Feature PRs still open | 3: #95 (#50) and #98 (#52), both open since Oct 17 with no review, and #122 (#5, 20 files) |
| Not started or still in progress | #63 and #64 (split into #117 and #118; #117 is in progress on its branch) |

**What went well**
- The availability-grid epic (#32) is finished end to end (#69–#73, #93), and the 2FA epic shipped as two clean sub-issues (#111, #112).
- Specs and PR descriptions improved: user stories, acceptance criteria, design alternatives and Tech Debt sections are the norm now (see #110, #113, #120).
- Splitting large issues worked when it was done early: #63 became #117 and #118, and #68 became #111 and #112.

**What didn't**
1. **Review bottleneck.** #95 and #98 waited about two weeks with no review, which is most of the reason #50 and #52 aren't done.
2. **Late merges.** #125 merged after the deadline, and several PRs merged in the last 24 hours.
3. **Issue/PR links drifted.** #114 didn't link #57, so the issue stayed open after the code shipped. #67 and #68 are still open although #111 and #112 delivered them. #13 is still open after #125 merged.
4. **Self-merges.** #113 and #120 were merged by their own author. The course rule is that you can't merge your own PR.
5. **PR size.** #113 and #120 went over the limit mainly because AI log transcripts were committed in the feature PR. #122 is 20 files.

## 2. Sprint 3 goals

1. **Finish what Sprint 2 started before taking new work.** Merge or close #95, #98 and #122 in week 1, and resolve #13.
2. **Close the recurrence feature (#23)** through #117, then #118, then #64.
3. **One or two new medium issues per member,** chosen from the existing backlog, which still has specs and difficulty estimates.
4. **Process:** no review waits more than 48 hours, nothing merges in the last 24 hours, and every merged PR closes its issue.

## 3. Proposed backlog

### Carry-overs (do first)

| Issue | Suggested owner | Pts | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|
| #50 Month calendar view for bookings | dbbeynam | 5 | Get #95 reviewed, rebase on `main`, merge |
| #52 Bulk cancel on bookings list | dbbeynam | 5 | Rebase #98 on #114 (soft-cancel) and #125 (waitlist), because all three change the cancel path. Re-test that bulk cancel works with the undo window and releases slots to the waitlist. |
| #5 Event theme | zach-short | 5 | Split #122 (20 files) into a backend PR (storage, validation) and an editor/booker UI PR |
| #13 Waitlist | zachbowden | — | Check #125 against the acceptance criteria, close #13 or open sub-issues for the rest |
| #117 Choose weekly recurrence days | dchan01-wm | 5 | Finish the branch, open a PR early in the sprint |
| #118 Offer only repeat days on booking page | dchan01-wm | 3 | Starts after #117 merges |
| #64 Recurrence end conditions | dchan01-wm | 5 | Decide how "Never" works (cap the series or change the model) in the spec before coding. It touches the same recurrence code as #117, so wait until #117 lands. |

### Housekeeping (no points)
- Close #67 and #68 as delivered by #111 and #112, and close #63 once #117 and #118 merge, with a comment linking the PRs.
- Comment on every Sprint 2 issue that isn't carried over, giving the reason.

### New work candidates (from the existing backlog)

| Issue | Pts | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| #12 `yarn build` silently migrates the database | 2 | Small and high-value: a safety fix for every developer. A good small issue for CSCI 535 scope. |
| #59 "Use different email" makes username unavailable | 3 | A bug; needs reproduction and a guard so verified usernames can't be taken |
| #35 Show durations ≥ 60 min as hours and minutes | 3 | Has an earlier closed PR (#61) to build on |
| #29 Live validation on signup | 3 | Has earlier closed PRs (#56, #58) to build on |
| #18 Recurring availability date overrides | 8 | Schema change; would build on the team's availability knowledge from #32 |
| #17 Availability schedule per event location | 8 | Touches the slot engine; split engine and UI work |
| #14 Insights dashboard | 8 | A chart library would be a new dependency and needs approval first |
| #33 AI search for settings | 8 | New external dependency and API keys; probably too risky for a final sprint |

**Suggested load:** finish the carry-overs, then each member picks enough from the table to meet the scope minimum (2 medium per CSCI 435 member). Prefer the 3–5 point issues over the 8s, since the 8-point issues would each need splitting to fit the PR size limit.

## 4. Process changes

| Problem in Sprint 2 | Change for Sprint 3 |
|---|---|
| PRs waited 2 weeks for review | Assign a reviewer when the PR opens (a rotation), post in Zulip, review within 24 hours and no longer than 48. Check unreviewed PRs at each stand-up. |
| Late merges | Internal deadline: all feature PRs open by the midpoint and merged 2 days before the due date. The last day is for docs, report and release only. |
| Issues not closed by PRs | Every feature PR body has `Closes #N`. Before the report, check that every merged PR's issue is closed. |
| Self-merges | Only the reviewer (or another teammate) merges. Consider enabling branch protection ("require 1 approval") on `main`. |
| AI logs inflate feature PRs | Commit AI logs in a separate `docs:` PR and link the specific log file in a comment on the issue or PR |
| Large PRs | Split by layer at planning time (backend PR, then UI PR) instead of after the PR is too large |
| Conflicts on shared code | Flag issues that touch the same area when planning: cancel path (#52, #57, #13) and recurrence (#117, #118, #64). Sequence those issues instead of running them in parallel. |

## 5. Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| End-of-semester workload compresses the sprint | High | Front-load carry-overs; keep new issues small or medium |
| Cancel-path changes conflict (#52 vs #57/#13) | Medium | Rebase #98 first thing; add a test covering bulk cancel plus soft-cancel |
| #64 "Never" needs a model change | Medium | Settle it in the spec. A capped series is the fallback. |
| New dependencies (#14, #33) don't get approved in time | Medium | Don't pick them unless approval comes in week 1 |
| Another release or report crunch | Medium | Draft the report from these tables mid-sprint; tag the release the day after the merge freeze |

## 6. Suggested timeline

| When | Milestone |
|---|---|
| Days 1–2 | Planning poker, owners assigned, `Sprint 3` milestone created, housekeeping closures done |
| Week 1 | #95, #98 and #122 (split) reviewed and merged; #13 resolved; #117 PR open; specs and design decisions written for new issues |
| Midpoint | Every issue has an open PR or a documented blocker; check-ins submitted |
| Due date minus 2 days | Merge freeze for feature PRs |
| Final 2 days | Diagrams, AI log PRs, report, release tag, reflection |

```
